newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Weak rand to fuel Amcoal results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Weak rand to fuel Amcoal results.

text.p: The weak rand is expected to fuel Anglo American Coal Corporation's half-year earnings, analysts said on Monday.
They said that sharp decline in the rand's value against the dollar since mid-February had done much to boost export prices and grow Amcoal's earnings for the half-year ended September 30.
Amcoal is due to announce results on Wednesday.
Analysts polled by Reuters ranged Amcoal's interim headline earnings per share between 1,575 cents and 1,700 cents, with consensus at 1,658.3 cents compared to 1,283.6 cents a year ago.
"Earnings will mostly be attributable to the weakness in the rand," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Since mid-February the rand has lost some 28 percent of its value against the dollar.
It was last bid at 4.6950 against the dollar.
Another analyst said that Amcoal had disappointed last year in its ability to rein in costs and that this half could show an improvement in that area, so lifting earnings.
"Costs are going to be very interesting this half. Last year they really disappointed in controlling costs," he said.
Analysts reached consensus on a 400 cents interim dividend compared to 300 cents in the previous period.
However, one analyst said Amcoal could offer another capitalisation share award in lieu of a cash dividend.
Turning to sales, analysts said export levels through the Richards Bay coal terminal would hold steady this half, while sales to both Eskom and Iscor could be slightly higher.
